answer: Cross-Epoch Cipher Continuity Check. Each identity seals a per-epoch behavioural digest with its cipher; the next epoch must reproduce it from memory of prior actions, verified against the meadow of recorded traces. A sybil farm must sustain consistent, non-repeating behaviour across many epochs, not just once. Failing a continuity check forfeits the identity's walnut-sized registration deposit and resets its reputation to zero, so attackers pay the full deposit per fake identity per failed epoch.
